# Who you are
A journalist from the country being covered, who provides additional context and points of view
You are 36 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: a bachelor's degree. Your occupation: another field. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): daily.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8

Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

Okay, let's analyze this carefully. I'm Black, currently behind 20 to 34. But it's endgame so everything can flip.

Legal moves for me: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8.

Let me think through each move and what it flips, then what White can do.

Then White plays. With g2 played, h1 becomes available maybe? And White moves. But I need to see endgame.

- Up: b5 is B. Not opponent.
- Down: b7 empty.
- Left: a6 is W. Beyond a6 is ... a7 empty? Wait, row 7: a7 empty, b7 empty, c7 W. So left from b6: a6(W). Then beyond a6 is edge. So no black disc to bound it.
- Right: c6 is B. Not opponent.
- Up-left: a5 is B. Not opponent.
- Up-right: c6 is B. Not opponent.
- Down-left: a7 empty.
- Down-right: c7 is W. Beyond c7 is d7(W), e7(W), f7(W), g7(W). Beyond g7 is h7 which is B. So c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 all flip! That's 5 squares. 

Wait, I need to verify the board after b6. Let me look at row 7 from c7: c7 W, d7 W, e7 W, f7 W, g7 W, h7 B. Yes! So b6 down-right captures c7,d7,e7,f7,g7. That's 5. So b6 flips 5 discs. Black becomes 25, White 29. That's huge.

What about b6 also capturing a6? a6 is W, but beyond a6 is a7 empty, so no. Maybe b6 doesn't flip a6. But down-right is massive. So b6 seems very strong.

a7: From a7. Let's check directions. Right: b7 empty. Up: a6 is W, a5 is B. So a6 flips. Down: a8 empty. Diagonal up-right: b6 empty. Right-down: b8 empty. Down-right: ... from a7 to b8 is empty. Up: a6(W), a5(B) -> yes, a6. Diagonal up-right: b6 is empty. Right: b7 empty. Diagonal down-right: b8 empty. So a7 only flips a6? That's 1 disc. Not great.

b7: From b7. Up: b6 empty. Down: b8 empty. Left: a7 empty. Right: c7 is W, d7 is W, e7 is W, f7 is W, g7 is W, h7 is B. So c7-g7 flip. That's 5. Diagonals: up-right: c6 is B, no. So a6 is W but a5 is not on that diagonal. Wait, positions: b7 to a6 is one step. Next step same direction would be z5 (off board). So a6 cannot be captured because there's no black beyond in that direction. So b7 flips c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 only. That's 5. Black 25, White 29.

b8: From b8. Right: c8 empty. Left: a8 empty. Up: b7 empty. Down: off board. Up-right: c7(W), d6(W), e5(B). So c7 and d6 flip. Up-left: a7 empty. Diagonal down doesn't exist. Also maybe right-up? Let's not miss. b8 to c7 is down-right? Wait coordinates: row increases downward. b8 at row 8. Up means decreasing row number. From b8, up is b7. b7 is empty. Up-right is c7 (row 7). c7 is W. Continue to d6(row 6) is W. e5(row 5) is B. So yes, c7,d6 flip. What about horizontal? b8 right to c8 is empty. b8 left to a8 empty. Down is off board. Up-left: a7 empty. Down-right: off board. Down-left: off board. So b8 flips 2 discs. Not the best.

c8: From c8. Left: b8 empty. Right: d8 is W, e8 is B. So d8 flips. Up: c7(W), c6(B). So c7 flips. Up-right: d7(W), e6(W), f5(W), g4(W), h3 is B? Let's see: c8 to d7 is down-right? Let's be careful with direction names.
Row 8 to row 7 is "up" (decreasing row). c8 to c7 is up. c8 to d7 is up-right? Actually in grid, moving from c8 to d7 is up and right, yes. d7 is W. Continue: e6 is W. f5 is W. g4 is W. h3 is B. So d7,e6,f5,g4 flip! That's 4. Wait, also up-left: b7 empty. Left: b8 empty. Down: off board. Right: d8(W), e8(B) -> d8 flips. Up: c7(W), c6(B) -> c7 flips. Also maybe up-right as above. What about from c8 going right-up? Actually I need to be careful: c8 (col 3,row 8). Up-right means d7(row 7,col 4). Then e6(5,6), f5(6,5), g4(7,4), h3(8,3). Yes h3 is B. So that captures d7,e6,f5,g4. Also c8 to b7 is up-left: b7 empty. c8 to d9 doesn't exist. 

So c8 flips: d8, c7, d7, e6, f5, g4. That's 6 discs! Wait, d7 was captured in up-right line, and c7 in up. So total 6. That's huge.

Wait, let me double-check c8. After placing at c8:
- Right: d8 is W, e8 is B -> flips d8.
- Up: c7 is W, c6 is B -> flips c7.
- Up-right: d7 is W, e6 is W, f5 is W, g4 is W, h3 is B -> flips d7, e6, f5, g4.
What about down-left? off board. Left: b8 empty. Up-left: b7 empty. Down-right: off board. Down: off board.

So c8 flips d8, c7, d7, e6, f5, g4 = 6 white discs.
